A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same material-taxonomy, Matador dataset, and hierarchical recognition study. The main text, supplementary Sections S1–S4, equations, tables, and figures are complete and readable.

before.justification: v1 reports original recognition experiments on existing benchmarks and Matador, including novel-view ablations, out-of-distribution evaluation, and few-shot learning.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and reports revised supplementary baseline results in Table S2.

M1.justification: The taxonomy-based GAT, node initialization, message passing, maximum-of-BCE-and-CE loss, novel-view rendering, and multiscale scene-probing procedure are retained. Calling the existing loss combination 'greedy' does not change its formula.

E1.justification: Both versions use KTH-TIPS2-b, FMD, GTOS, GTOS-Mobile, Matador, and Matador-C1. Color, grayscale, context-derived OOD, scene-probing, and held-out-material few-shot scenarios already appear in v1.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within Table 1, Figure 5a, and Table S2. Table S2 shortens 'Ours (ResNet50)' to 'Ours', while its caption still specifies ResNet50; revised baseline scores do not introduce different comparators.

E3.justification: Section S2.2 changes vignetting correction from an optional operation supported by code to an applied preprocessing step. The strength-label threshold for Figure 6 changes from 5 MPa to 1 MPa. These are limited reported setting revisions; the PDFs do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Table S2 revises the evidence from the head-only versus end-to-end fine-tuning comparison: identical color scores across these regimes in v1 become substantial gaps in v3. The analysis design and the other novel-view, grayscale, confusion-matrix, scene-probing, and few-shot analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains the same uncertainty reporting. Neither version adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or a different uncertainty-estimation procedure; the Monte Carlo dropout description is also unchanged.

E6.justification: Table S2 substantially revises head-only color accuracy: DeepTEN 88.8→54.0, DEPNet 87.6→76.8, FRP 89.4→68.9, and MSLac 88.5→79.1, changing their ranking and separation from end-to-end training. Table S3 adds Poisson's ratios and extensively revises literature-derived property ranges, with corresponding updates in Figure 1d. These substantially change the supplementary quantitative record, although Table 1 and Figure 5 recognition results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The formal graph construction, message-passing equation, training loss, rendering assumptions, and Equations S1–S6 are mathematically unchanged. The added practical shear-strength approximation does not introduce a derivation, proof, or revised formal analysis.

C1.justification: The abstract is unchanged in substance, and the introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning the taxonomy, dataset, hierarchical recognition, OOD generalization, and few-shot adaptation.

C2.justification: Table S3 adds guidance for estimating shear strength as one-half of tensile strength for brittle materials and three-fifths for ductile materials. Several property entries now refer to textiles or pelts rather than individual fibers. The main interpretations of recognition results and applicability limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Sections S2.2–S2.3 newly specify Mitchell-Netravali filtering for enlargement and Lanczos filtering for reduction. These disclose previously unspecified implementation choices. Network dimensions, training hyperparameters, hardware, training-time information, and Matador access remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The supplement adds an ImageMagick reference and usage-guide citation supporting the resampling discussion. The remaining cited works and the paper's positioning relative to material recognition and hierarchical learning are retained.

P1.justification: v3 corrects spelling, grammar, capitalization, and terminology, shortens the affiliation, and lightly rewrites dataset and implementation descriptions. The section organization and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Several existing plots and annotations are redrawn with sharper text and adjusted spacing. Table S2 gains an explicit accuracy header, and Table S3 gains a Poisson's-ratio column with reformatted headers. The figure set and overall document layout are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves reproducibility through explicit resampling choices and improves figure and table legibility. Table S2 replaces duplicated head-only color entries with distinct reported results. The core method and principal empirical evidence remain unchanged, while the expanded mechanical-property table remains approximate and lacks per-entry source attribution, limiting the benefit of that expansion.
